research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK, Defra/UK-AIR, Environment Agency, Natural England and LAQM verification; 2026 currentness where available; AQMA/monitoring/modelled data, planning-vs-permitting, application-vs-decision, permit-vs-compliance, noise/statutory-nuisance and odour-management separation. Not parcel-level air-quality, noise or permit accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Planning practice guidance: Air quality
official_sources.fact: MHCLG planning guidance explains how development-management decisions can account for air-quality impacts and the level of assessment needed.
official_sources.gate: Air-quality relevance or an AQMA is not an automatic refusal or parcel-level exceedance result.

official_sources.name: Planning practice guidance: Noise
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance requires noise to be considered where development creates noise or is sensitive to the prevailing acoustic environment.
official_sources.gate: Noise relevance is not a measured site impact or planning refusal without proposal- and receptor-specific evidence.

official_sources.name: Air quality strategy framework for local authority delivery
official_sources.fact: The strategy describes local monitoring, Annual Status Reports, AQMAs and Air Quality Action Plans.
official_sources.gate: AQMA designation or an action plan does not prove a target parcel exceeds an objective or cannot be developed.

official_sources.name: Local Air Quality Management statutory directions
official_sources.fact: Secretary of State directions require specified authorities to review air quality annually or produce action plans.
official_sources.gate: An authority reporting duty is not parcel-specific concentration, exceedance or planning status.

official_sources.name: LAQM Technical Guidance TG22
official_sources.fact: Current LAQM technical guidance supports evidence-based local-authority air-quality assessment and action planning.
official_sources.gate: A methodology or screening tool is not an exact parcel measurement or planning determination.

official_sources.name: LAQM Background Maps
official_sources.fact: Defra background maps provide modelled estimates of background pollutant concentrations for LAQM assessment.
official_sources.gate: Modelled background concentration is not a site monitor reading or total proposal-specific concentration.

official_sources.name: AURN air pollution monitoring
official_sources.fact: Defra's AURN provides quality-controlled high-resolution near-real-time measurements from monitoring stations.
official_sources.gate: A monitoring-station reading must not be treated as the exact concentration at a different parcel.

official_sources.name: Air pollution in the UK monitoring data sources
official_sources.fact: Defra identifies official monitoring networks and how their air-pollution data are published.
official_sources.gate: Network coverage is not proof that every parcel has a colocated monitor or verified local concentration.

official_sources.name: DEFRA UK-AIR home and measurement summary
official_sources.fact: UK-AIR publishes current forecasts and provisional measurement summaries using Environment Agency data.
official_sources.gate: Regional/current provisional measurements are not a parcel-specific annual compliance determination.

official_sources.name: DEFRA UK-AIR pollution forecast
official_sources.fact: UK-AIR publishes up-to-five-day pollution forecasts and location searches.
official_sources.gate: Forecast pollution bands are not measured historic exposure, planning assessment or permit compliance.

official_sources.name: DEFRA UK-AIR modelled background pollution data
official_sources.fact: Defra publishes modelled background pollution maps at 1 km resolution for policy and research uses.
official_sources.gate: A 1 km model grid is not exact parcel concentration and must not replace a site-specific assessment where required.

official_sources.name: Natural England air pollution and development advice
official_sources.fact: Natural England standing advice sets steps for assessing air-pollution effects of planning proposals on protected sites.
official_sources.gate: Standing advice or screening distance is not an adverse-effect conclusion without the proposal, protected site and in-combination evidence.

official_sources.name: Apply for an environmental permit
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance sets the 2026 application route for environmental permits in England.
official_sources.gate: Submitting an environmental-permit application is not a granted permit, planning permission or operational compliance.

official_sources.name: Check if you need an environmental permit
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance separates permit, exclusion and exemption routes and the relevant regulator.
official_sources.gate: A permit category or exemption route is not evidence that a particular operator is authorised or compliant.

official_sources.name: Environmental permit pre-application advice
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency pre-application advice helps applicants identify permit requirements and environmental issues.
official_sources.gate: Pre-application advice is not permit approval, planning approval or a guarantee of determination outcome.

official_sources.name: Environment Agency Public Registers Online
official_sources.fact: The Environment Agency public register exposes permits, licences, exemptions and available compliance assessment reports.
official_sources.gate: A register hit identifies a regulatory record; it does not prove current planning status, all compliance history or parcel-wide impacts.

official_sources.name: Environmental public registers collection
official_sources.fact: The National Data Library collection describes searchable and downloadable Environment Agency environmental public-register data.
official_sources.gate: A downloadable register is discovery evidence and requires exact permit, operator, address and status matching.

official_sources.name: Environmental permit applications: list of decisions
official_sources.fact: The Environment Agency publishes permit decision lists and directs users to final permits on public registers.
official_sources.gate: An application listing is not a final permit; an issued decision still requires exact permit scope and current status.

official_sources.name: IED environmental permits issued collection
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency collections provide permits and decision documents issued under the Industrial Emissions framework.
official_sources.gate: Collection membership is not proof that a target parcel is affected or that a permit remains unchanged/current.

official_sources.name: IED environmental permits issued 2026 S to Z
official_sources.fact: The 2026 collection contains current permit, variation and surrender decisions, including decisions dated July 2026.
official_sources.gate: A decision date/type must be read with the exact permit; variation or surrender cannot be collapsed into generic site authorisation.

official_sources.name: Best available techniques for environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Updated January 2026, the guidance explains BAT requirements and derogations for environmental permits.
official_sources.gate: BAT applicability or a BAT conclusion is not itself a permit or site-specific compliance finding.

official_sources.name: UK BAT
official_sources.fact: UK BAT describes the system for developing BAT conclusions used as a basis for industrial permit conditions.
official_sources.gate: A BAT conclusion is a standards input, not proof of a site's permit conditions or compliance outcome.

official_sources.name: Industrial emissions modernising environmental permitting
official_sources.fact: The April 2026 government response sets the direction for further detailed reform of industrial permitting.
official_sources.gate: Consultation outcome and future policy are not current parcel permits or automatic changes to existing authorisations.

official_sources.name: Standard rules environmental permitting
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency standard-rules permits define fixed rules and risk assessments for eligible activities and were updated in 2026.
official_sources.gate: Availability of standard rules does not prove an activity qualifies, has a permit or meets site-specific constraints.

official_sources.name: Medium combustion plant permit application
official_sources.fact: Updated March 2026, guidance covers standard and bespoke MCP permits and screening requirements.
official_sources.gate: MCP permit application or screening does not cover planning permission or every environmental impact.

official_sources.name: Specified generator permit application
official_sources.fact: Updated February 2026, guidance explains specified-generator permits and their air-emission scope.
official_sources.gate: A specified-generator permit covers defined air emissions and must not be treated as approval for water, land, odour, noise or planning matters.

official_sources.name: Medium combustion plant and specified generator regulations
official_sources.fact: The collection links current permit, applicability and compliance guidance for MCP and specified generators.
official_sources.gate: Regime applicability is not a parcel-specific permit, emission result or development consent.

official_sources.name: A1 installations environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance identifies A1 industrial installations and standard/bespoke permit routes.
official_sources.gate: A process category is not evidence that a particular site operates that process or holds a live permit.

official_sources.name: Local authority environmental permits
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK identifies local-authority permits for Part A2 and Part B activities and mobile plant.
official_sources.gate: A Part A2/B category or local regulator is not proof of a live permit or acceptable planning impact.

official_sources.name: Local Authority Pollution Control general guidance manual
official_sources.fact: Defra guidance explains policy and procedures for local-authority A2 and Part B pollution control.
official_sources.gate: The regulatory manual is not site-specific authorisation, compliance or planning evidence.

official_sources.name: Environmental permitting resources for local authorities
official_sources.fact: Defra collects risk methods, permits, guidance and charging materials used by local-authority pollution-control regulators.
official_sources.gate: Resource availability does not demonstrate that a particular installation is permitted or compliant.

official_sources.name: Noise and vibration management environmental permits publication
official_sources.fact: Updated May 2026, Environment Agency guidance covers noise impact assessment, management plans and permit compliance.
official_sources.gate: A requirement for noise assessment is not a finding of significant adverse impact or statutory nuisance.

official_sources.name: Noise and vibration management environmental permits detailed guidance
official_sources.fact: The detailed guidance sets a staged assessment process including monitoring, source assessment, context and uncertainty.
official_sources.gate: Desktop screening or modelled noise cannot be promoted to exact receptor impact without the required assessment evidence.

official_sources.name: Statutory nuisances: council complaint handling
official_sources.fact: Defra guidance explains when noise, smoke, odour, artificial light and other matters may amount to statutory nuisance and when abatement notices apply.
official_sources.gate: A complaint is not a statutory-nuisance determination or an abatement notice.

official_sources.name: Artificial light nuisance guidance
official_sources.fact: Defra guidance explains artificial-light statutory nuisance, exemptions and council assessment duties.
official_sources.gate: Light presence or a complaint is not proof of statutory nuisance, planning breach or required mitigation.

official_sources.name: Complain about noise to the council
official_sources.fact: GOV.UK explains council investigation and abatement action where statutory noise nuisance is established.
official_sources.gate: A noise complaint or investigation is not an abatement order or parcel development constraint.

official_sources.name: Outdoor equipment noise regulations
official_sources.fact: Updated February 2026, guidance covers regulated outdoor equipment noise labels, sound-power documentation and conformity.
official_sources.gate: Equipment conformity data is not a site acoustic assessment or planning-noise conclusion.

official_sources.name: Odour management: definition of odour pollution
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance defines the regulatory concept of odour pollution for permitted activities.
official_sources.gate: Odour potential or perception is not a permit breach, statutory nuisance or exact off-site impact without evidence.

official_sources.name: Odour management: permit condition
official_sources.fact: The guidance explains standard odour permit conditions and when an approved odour management plan may be required.
official_sources.gate: An approved management plan does not prove all equipment or operational details are sufficient or that no odour events can occur.

official_sources.name: Odour management: assessing odorous emissions
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance covers proportionate monitoring and assessment of odorous emissions under permits.
official_sources.gate: Odour monitoring methodology is not proof of a site's current emission level or off-site effect.

official_sources.name: Odour management plan guidance
official_sources.fact: The 2025 guidance requires site-specific risks, auditable controls, monitoring and review in odour management plans.
official_sources.gate: A submitted or approved plan is not evidence of zero odour impact or full permit compliance.

official_sources.name: Control and monitor emissions for environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance covers emission controls, limits, monitoring and plans for odour, noise, vibration and pests.
official_sources.gate: A management-system requirement or monitoring plan is not a measured compliance result.

official_sources.name: Risk assessments for environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance separates screening from detailed modelling and requires risk assessments with permit applications.
official_sources.gate: Worst-case screening or an H1 result is not an exact parcel concentration, planning decision or permit grant.

official_sources.name: Air emissions risk assessment for environmental permits
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance explains process contribution, predicted environmental concentration, screening and detailed dispersion modelling.
official_sources.gate: A screened or modelled PC/PEC must not be treated as observed concentration or planning acceptability without the proper context.

official_sources.name: Environment Agency permit consultations
official_sources.fact: The Environment Agency publishes open consultations on live environmental-permit applications and variations.
official_sources.gate: An open consultation is an application-stage record, not an issued permit or evidence of final conditions.

official_sources.name: Environmental permit compliance assessment scoring
official_sources.fact: Updated June 2026, Environment Agency guidance explains how permit compliance is assessed, scored and reflected in compliance records.
official_sources.gate: A compliance score or CAR is time- and scope-specific and does not replace the current permit, full enforcement history or planning status.
